meaning: The number 130 is linked to Adam's age when he fathered his son Seth, symbolizing a new beginning after the fall and the loss of Abel.
description: In Genesis 5:3 it is stated that Adam was 130 years old when he fathered Seth, who became the ancestor of the righteous line leading to Noah. The name Seth means "placed in the stead", marking God’s faithfulness by giving a new beginning after the loss of Abel. In Jewish tradition, the number is also connected with Jacob, who gave his age as 130 years when he met Pharaoh in Egypt (Genesis 47:9). Jacob himself described his years as "few and hard", and this meeting marked the beginning of Israel’s stay in Egypt—a transitional period with great consequences in salvation history. Also the high priest Jehoiada lived to be 130 years old (2 Chronicles 24:15), a man who preserved faithfulness to the Lord during a time of apostasy. The number 130 thus carries symbolism linked to trials, faithfulness, and renewal in times of transition.

versions.description: In Genesis 5:3 it is stated that Adam was 130 years old when he fathered Seth, who became the ancestor of the righteous line leading to Noah. In Jewish tradition, the number is also associated with Jacob, who gave his age as 130 years when he met Pharaoh in Egypt (Genesis 47:9), marking the beginning of Israel's stay in Egypt. Some rabbinic sources reflect on the 130 years Adam allegedly lived separated from Eve after being driven out of Eden's garden, as a period of repentance and remorse. The number thus carries symbolism connected to trials, renewal, and transitions in salvation history.
versions.reason: [minor] 2 Chronicles 24:15 mentions Jehoiada who lived to be 130 years old – this is a relevant biblical reference missing from the description; [minor] The rabbinic tradition about Adam's 130 years separated from Eve is an interesting addition, but it somewhat disrupts the flow of the main text and would fit better as a footnote; [minor] Jacob's description of his years as 'few and hard' is an important part of the context in Genesis 47:9 that could well be included to strengthen the symbolism about trials.

footnotes.text: According to rabbinic tradition (Eruvin 18b), Adam lived separated from Eve for 130 years after being driven out of the Garden of Eden, as a period of repentance and sorrow before Seth was born.

The gematria value of the Hebrew word "sulam" (סֻלָּם, ladder) – as in Jacob's dream in Genesis 28:12 – is 130, the same as "Sinai" (סיני). Rabbinic sources see this as a connection between Jacob's revelation and the giving of the law at Sinai.
